Series::is_leaf¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

bool Series::is_leaf() const

What It Does¶

Returns true when the Series is a leaf of the reverse-mode graph — that is, when it has no recorded operation that produced it — and false when it is an interior result computed from other tracked tensors.

Concretely:

  • A Series you created directly (make_series, zeros, a parameter you built) is a leaf, whether or not it tracks slope.

  • The result of any op on a slope-tracking input (x.square(), a.matmul(b), …) is not a leaf — it carries a source link back to its parents.

  • detach() severs that link, so a detached view of an interior result is a leaf again.

Leaf status is about graph provenance, nothing else. It is independent of rank, dtype, platform, whether the tensor currently holds a sensitivity, and — importantly — independent of tracks_slope(): a leaf can track slope (a trainable parameter) or not (a plain constant), and an interior result tracks slope while never being a leaf.

Why it matters: after reverse(), sensitivity is retained automatically only on leaves — they are the natural optimization targets (weights, inputs you are differentiating with respect to). To keep an interior result’s sensitivity you must ask for it explicitly with retain_grad().

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

bool true iff the Series has no source link (it was created directly, or detached), false if it was produced by a recorded op.

Gradient¶

Not applicable — is_leaf() returns a plain bool. (It describes the graph; it is not part of it.)

Examples¶

Example 1. A plain, untracked Series is a leaf — leaf-ness does not require slope tracking.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "untracked: is_leaf=" << x.is_leaf()
          << " tracks_slope=" << x.tracks_slope() << "\n";

Output¶

untracked: is_leaf=true tracks_slope=false

Example 2. A tracked user tensor is a leaf; a value computed from it is not — even though both track slope.

auto leaf = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
leaf.tracks_slope_(true);
auto result = leaf.square();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "leaf:   is_leaf=" << leaf.is_leaf()   << " tracks_slope=" << leaf.tracks_slope()   << "\n"
          << "result: is_leaf=" << result.is_leaf() << " tracks_slope=" << result.tracks_slope() << "\n";

Output¶

leaf:   is_leaf=true tracks_slope=true
result: is_leaf=false tracks_slope=true

This is the distinction to keep straight: is_leaf() and tracks_slope() are orthogonal. result tracks slope (its gradient will flow) but it is not a leaf (it has parents).

Example 3. detach() makes an interior result a leaf again by cutting its link to the graph.

auto leaf = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
leaf.tracks_slope_(true);
auto result = leaf.square();
auto d = result.detach();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "result.is_leaf()          = " << result.is_leaf() << "\n"
          << "result.detach().is_leaf() = " << d.is_leaf() << "\n";

Output¶

result.is_leaf()          = false
result.detach().is_leaf() = true

d shares result’s values but has no history — a useful way to feed a computed quantity into a fresh graph as a constant.

Example 4. Only leaves keep sensitivity automatically after reverse().

auto w = pluss::make_series({2.0, 3.0});
w.tracks_slope_(true);
auto y = w.mul(w);            // interior result, not a leaf
y.sum().reverse();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "w.is_leaf()=" << w.is_leaf()
          << " has_sensitivity=" << w.has_sensitivity() << "\n"
          << "y.is_leaf()=" << y.is_leaf()
          << " has_sensitivity=" << y.has_sensitivity() << "\n";

Output¶

w.is_leaf()=true has_sensitivity=true
y.is_leaf()=false has_sensitivity=false

w (a leaf) has its sensitivity; y (interior) does not — call y.retain_grad() before reverse() if you need it.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • is_leaf() is not tracks_slope(). A leaf can be untracked (a constant); an interior result can track slope. They answer different questions.

  • After reverse(), sensitivity is retained only on leaves. Use retain_grad() for an interior result you need the gradient of.

  • detach() produces a leaf; the original interior result is unchanged and stays non-leaf.

  • Suspending recording (no_grad) changes whether new ops acquire history — it does not retroactively turn an existing interior result into a leaf.

Summary¶

is_leaf() reports a Series’ position in the reverse-mode graph:

  • true for a directly created tensor (tracked or not) and for a detach()ed view

  • false for the result of any op on a slope-tracking input

  • orthogonal to tracks_slope()

  • leaves keep their sensitivity automatically after reverse(); interior results need retain_grad()

See Also¶

  • Series::tracks_slope: whether gradient flows through this tensor — the orthogonal question.

  • Series::retain_grad: keep an interior result’s sensitivity past reverse().

  • Series::detach: produce a history-free (leaf) view.

  • Series::reverse: the reverse pass whose retained sensitivities land on leaves.
